nodes.label: Build once, promote always
nodes.rationale: Rebuilding per environment invites "works in staging" drift; the artifact that passed main verification should be the same bytes deployed to every downstream environment.

nodes.label: Three-layer pipeline model (PR / main / release)
nodes.rationale: Separating PR validation, main/trunk verification, and release/promotion makes the separation of concerns visible even when layers share a file, and keeps the build-once/promote-always discipline enforceable.

nodes.label: Trunk-based development default
nodes.rationale: Short-lived PR branches merged to a single mainline are preferred over long-lived GitFlow release branches, consistent with DORA-oriented delivery research and most modern CI designs.

nodes.label: Least-privilege workflow permissions
nodes.rationale: Set a workflow-level read-only permissions floor and grant write scopes only on the specific jobs that need them, so a compromised step cannot push code, mint releases, or change settings.

nodes.label: Blocking vs advisory gates
nodes.rationale: Rolling a new scanner out as advisory first is fine; leaving it advisory forever without a plan is a finding at standard+ maturity — required status checks should match the blocking set.

nodes.rationale: The <10 threshold is traceable directly to mccabe's own README rather than an arbitrary judgment call; Ruff's C901 category is opt-in, not default-on, so complexity checking is often silently absent.

nodes.label: Deadlock Scope Correction
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_database.deadlocks is checked by MCPg under the Concurrency & Lock Contention audit_database category, which mcpg-tooling.md's mapping assigns to Workload & query performance, not Health — the reference must not duplicate this finding across domains.

nodes.label: USING/WITH CHECK Auto-Inherit Rule
nodes.rationale: A bare USING clause on UPDATE/ALL policies is auto-inherited as WITH CHECK when omitted — the real exploit shape is narrower than 'any policy without explicit WITH CHECK is a hole': only an INSERT policy (no USING fallback) or an explicit too-permissive WITH CHECK actually opens a gap.

nodes.label: pg_blocking_pids() Blocking-Chain Pattern
nodes.rationale: Official Postgres guidance recommends pg_blocking_pids() over a raw pg_locks self-join because such a join 'would have to encode knowledge about which lock modes conflict with which others' and the view doesn't expose wait-queue ordering.

nodes.label: New Domain: Dependency & Supply Chain Security
nodes.norm_label: new domain: dependency & supply chain security
nodes.rationale: Distinct reviewer lens from Security (is this code's logic exploitable) and Standards Compliance (is build/tooling config correct): asks whether the artifacts, dependencies, and pipeline that produce this code can be trusted or tampered with. Grounded in SLSA Build Track and OWASP CI/CD Security Top 10.

nodes.label: Reporting Absence as a Finding
nodes.rationale: This domain's distinctive job is flagging patterns that don't exist at all (zero circuit breakers, zero timeouts) as findings in their own right, since the risk is latent until the first outage rather than visible in a stack trace.

nodes.label: Dataclasses vs Pydantic Decision Rule
nodes.rationale: Sourced decision rule: use pydantic.BaseModel for data crossing a trust boundary (validation is the point), plain dataclasses for internal already-typed data (validation is pure overhead). Plain dicts are the anti-pattern either way.

nodes.label: Walrus Operator: PEP 572's Own Style Guidance
nodes.norm_label: walrus operator: pep 572's own style guidance
nodes.rationale: PEP 572 itself prefers a plain assignment statement when either form works, and directs restructuring wherever the walrus form creates ambiguity about execution order — a more actionable bar than a generic readability gut-check.

nodes.label: Three Disagreeing Wraparound Scales
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL's own 40M/3M thresholds, MCPg's 80M/150M, and pganalyze's percentage-of-2B framing are all legitimate but different risk appetites on the same age(datfrozenxid) number; the review must trust MCPg's own live output as what fires, not an external doc's number.

nodes.label: vacuum_failsafe_age
nodes.rationale: Default 1.6 billion transactions (~75% to the hard wraparound limit) — VACUUM's last resort, dropping cost-based delay and skipping non-essential index cleanup to race the wraparound clock; not previously covered in the thin v0 doc at all.

nodes.label: Checkpoint & Background-Writer Behavior
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 17 split checkpoint counters out of pg_stat_bgwriter into a new pg_stat_checkpointer view, so findings must confirm server version before trusting a raw pg_stat_bgwriter-only query on PG17+.

nodes.label: Health & Configuration Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Scopes the domain to instance-level health independent of schema/query specifics; deliberately excludes capacity planning and hardware selection; hands bloat remediation to Maintenance and deadlocks/lock contention to Workload rather than duplicating them.

nodes.label: Transaction ID Wraparound
nodes.rationale: Three disagreeing severity scales exist for the same age(datfrozenxid) number (Postgres's own 40M/3M, MCPg's 80M/150M, pganalyze's percentage framing); the doc directs trusting MCPg's own live output as what drives review severity rather than an external doc's number.

nodes.label: Maintenance Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Owns the vacuum/bloat/sequence mechanism but deliberately not the live wraparound-proximity check (age(datfrozenxid)), which belongs to Health & configuration; this domain explains why wraparound risk accumulates without duplicating Health's scored proximity check.

nodes.label: Wraparound Mechanism (Maintenance Angle)
nodes.rationale: Explains freeze thresholds and the emergency failsafe (the mechanism preventing wraparound) as complementary to, not a restatement of, Health's live proximity check.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements Activation Requirement
nodes.rationale: Activation is a config-and-restart step (shared_preload_libraries), not just CREATE EXTENSION — an operator who only ran CREATE EXTENSION still has an empty view, indistinguishable from 'not installed' to a downstream reviewer, which is why a Not-Implemented fallback exists at all.

nodes.label: audit_database Category → Domain Mapping
nodes.rationale: audit_database's single composite call fans its CategoryResults out across four of the seven domains; each must dedupe against that domain's dedicated tools rather than double-counting the same underlying issue.

nodes.label: Workload & Query Performance Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Top consumers and pathological patterns using MCPg-gatherable evidence (pg_stat_statements, live plan/lock snapshots) — not rewriting application code or a full query inventory.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements Unavailable → Not Implemented
nodes.rationale: When pg_stat_statements is unavailable, the domain scores Not Implemented rather than inventing a clean-workload conclusion from live-pressure tools alone — reporting 9-10 here would misrepresent absence of evidence as a clean bill of health.

nodes.label: Database Role Segregation (3-user pattern)
nodes.rationale: OWASP's Database Security Cheat Sheet establishes least-privilege but does not prescribe a specific role count; the readonly/writer/admin 3-user split is this research's own reasoned elaboration, explicitly labeled as such rather than a named standard.

nodes.label: Worker Count Formula (2×CPU+1)
nodes.rationale: Gunicorn's own docs state (2×CPU)+1 as a starting formula, then immediately qualify it ('4-12 workers typically enough'); flag deployments with no reasoning at all, not deviation from the formula's exact output.

nodes.label: Write/Vacuum/WAL Cost of Index Set
nodes.rationale: Every index is maintained on every write touching an indexed column; write cost scales with index count not just write volume, and autovacuum must process every index during bulk-delete and cleanup phases — the mechanism behind favoring a lean index set.

nodes.label: License Choice + ADR Offer (Phase 4 / Phase 8)
nodes.rationale: SKILL.md mandates always offering an ADR after a real architecture-template decision, even for small projects — never silently skipping the offer because a project 'seems too small.'

nodes.label: Log Injection: the Structural Angle
nodes.rationale: Structured logging only closes log-forging when paired with an escaping renderer (JSON) in production; a structlog app on ConsoleRenderer keeps the exposure open despite using a structured library.

nodes.label: Decision Log
nodes.rationale: Records why each of the seven reference docs was independently re-researched against live PostgreSQL docs and MCPg source rather than the abbreviated docs/tools.md index, surfacing corrections like RLS bypass mechanics and a previously-unlisted duplicate/redundant-index check.

nodes.label: run_advisors Tool-Map Gap Finding
nodes.rationale: Indexing's original tool list had no tool detecting duplicate/redundant indexes; that check actually lives in run_advisors' _duplicate_indexes/_redundant_indexes rules — a correction surfaced here rather than silently patched into mcpg-tooling.md.

nodes.label: run_advisors Six Rules (Verified)
nodes.rationale: run_advisors already implements exactly the rules this domain needs (missing_primary_key, unindexed_foreign_key, duplicate_indexes, nullable_timestamp_without_tz, recommend_graph_indices, redundant_indexes), deliberately conservative by the module's own docstring — 'would a careful reviewer flag this?' not 'is this provably wrong?'.

nodes.label: Hygiene & Conventions Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Deliberately the lightest domain: flags inconsistency and dead weight rather than enforcing one 'correct' style; most findings are Minor by design.

nodes.label: Indexing Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Every index is a standing bet that read benefit outweighs write/cache/vacuum/WAL cost; the domain audits whether that bet still pays off, not whether more indexes exist.

nodes.label: Schema Integrity Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Structural soundness of keys/FK graph/partition sanity — not product data modeling or green-field redesign; audit_database does not cover this domain, it relies entirely on its own dedicated tools.

nodes.label: Dedup Rule Verification
nodes.rationale: Confirms find_unused_objects returns both zero-scan tables and indexes in one call with no pre-split by domain — the Hygiene/Indexing split is inferred from the tour description plus the baseline's own dual listing, not from a deeper MCPg spec.

nodes.label: Dedup Rule vs. Indexing
nodes.rationale: find_unused_objects returns both zero-scan tables and zero-scan indexes in one call; split by object type not by tool — indexes go to Indexing (write/vacuum/WAL cost angle), tables stay in Hygiene (clutter/ops-confusion angle) — never double-report the same object.

nodes.label: Worked Example: RLS Enabled Not Forced
nodes.norm_label: worked example: rls enabled not forced

nodes.label: FORCE RLS Only Closes Owner Bypass
nodes.norm_label: force rls only closes owner bypass
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL docs state superuser/BYPASSRLS 'always' bypass row security with no stated exception for FORCE; FORCE is documented purely as an opt-in for the owner's own queries — a reviewer seeing FORCE set might wrongly conclude RLS is airtight when a BYPASSRLS app role still walks through it.

nodes.label: Invalid Indexes & CONCURRENTLY Rationale
nodes.rationale: CONCURRENTLY avoids the exclusive lock of a plain CREATE/DROP INDEX by splitting the build across transactions, at the cost of longer wall-clock time and leaving an invalid index behind on failure rather than rolling back cleanly.

nodes.label: Security & Access Domain Intent
nodes.rationale: Least-privilege smell tests, RLS posture, sensitive-column heuristics, connection-encryption signals — not a full CIS benchmark or secret-manager evaluation; also owns audit_database's Authentication & Password Hygiene category.

nodes.label: RLS Bypass Mechanics (FORCE limitations)
nodes.rationale: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY only removes the table-owner bypass exemption; superuser and BYPASSRLS roles bypass RLS unconditionally regardless of FORCE — a FORCE'd table must not be read as fully closed if the app role also carries BYPASSRLS or superuser.

nodes.label: Workflow Orchestration: Durable Execution vs DAG
nodes.norm_label: workflow orchestration: durable execution vs dag

nodes.label: Middleware Domain-Boundary Correction
nodes.rationale: Most middleware controls (CORS, JWT/auth, rate limiting) are already Security's explicit checklist items; Architecture keeps only the structural presence/wiring check and cross-references Security for correctness rather than duplicating it.

nodes.label: Expansion: Security LLM Coverage Beyond Prompt Injection
nodes.norm_label: expansion: security llm coverage beyond prompt injection

nodes.label: New Domain: Concurrency & Async Correctness
nodes.rationale: Distinct from Performance (is it fast): asks is it correct under concurrent execution (races, deadlocks, cancellation bugs). Grounded in Ruff's flake8-async (ASYNC) category and PEP 703 free-threading obligations.

nodes.label: Concurrency Narrowed to Throughput/GIL Bottleneck
nodes.rationale: Performance keeps only the throughput question (is the concurrency model capable of speedup at all — GIL serializes CPU-bound threaded code); correctness-under-concurrency (races, deadlocks, async correctness) moves to the sibling Concurrency & Async Correctness domain per the scoping doc's explicit boundary.

nodes.label: Critical-Workload-Not-Implemented Grading Criteria
nodes.rationale: Requires the Critical RLS/BYPASSRLS finding first in severity order, an overall FAIL verdict, and Workload scored Not Implemented rather than a fabricated 9-10 'no hotspots' score when pg_stat_statements is missing.

nodes.label: Degraded-Mode-With-Consent Grading Criteria
nodes.rationale: Requires confirmed explicit consent before downgrading, catalog-only tool use, advisor-quality items marked Not Implemented, and the run plainly labeled degraded — never presented as equivalent to a full MCPg review.

nodes.label: Degraded Mode (Explicit Consent)
nodes.rationale: If MCPg readiness cannot pass, falling back to pg_catalog/information_schema/pg_stat_* is allowed only with explicit user consent; confidence must be marked reduced and never labeled as a full MCPg review.

nodes.label: CI/CD: Well-Formed, Not Secure
nodes.rationale: This domain owns whether CI/CD exists and is well-formed (test/lint stage exists and actually runs, fails build on non-zero exit); pipeline security (pinned actions, credential hygiene) is the sibling Dependency & Supply Chain Security domain's lens.
